Kuṇḍalinī
(‘the coiled one’)
------------------------------------------
See CAKRAS and TANTRAS.

Kuṇḍikopaniṣad
------------------------------------------
Classed among the minor उपनिषद्स्, the Kuṇḍikopaniṣad of the Sāmaveda deals entirely with सṁन्यास or monastic life. There are 34 verses, almost all in the anuṣṭubh metre.
After completing the first stage of ब्रह्मचर्य by studying the वेदस् under a competent teacher, a person has to marry a suitable girl and settle down as a होउसे-holder. Once the various duties of the householder’s life are fulfilled, he has to distribute his property among his sons and take to the life of a वानप्रस्थ or forest-recluse. In this stage, he has to lead a very austere life depending upon air or water or roots and fruits of the forest for living.
Once his वैराग्य or spirit of renunciation becomes ripened, he should decide to embrace the monastic life. In this way of life, he should totally give up all actions (including the Vedic fires themselves) and dedicate himself to the realisation of the आत्मन्/Brahman (the Self of all) by the repetition of the well-known Upaniṣadic महावाक्यस्. He must also adopt the monk’s way of life by wearing the red-robes and keeping a few necessary things like the kuṇḍikā or कमण्डलु (water-pot), a cup made of the coconut shell, cloth for filtering water, footwear, a loin-cloth, an upper cloth and a blanket.
He should—when not travelling—stay at temples or river-banks and other (deserted) places.
He should never care for the comforts or discomforts of the body nor for the praise or blame of people.
If he cannot follow the path of ज्ञान as described in the वेदस्, he can practise the योग of rousing the कुण्डलिनी.
If he realises the आत्मन् here and now, he will become a jīvanmukta and enjoy great bliss.
Otherwise, he gets क्रममुक्ति or gradual लिबेरतिओन् by leaving the body through the ब्रह्मरन्ध्र (aperture in the cranium) and passing through the देवयान.
The Upaniṣad ends with a brief description of the brahmajñāni’s subjective experience.
See also UPANIṢADS.
